recommended_text.methods: After completion of the frozen transfer evaluation, we inspected the archived CSP predictions for class imbalance and probability asymmetry. These descriptive checks used the original stored predictions and their ground-truth labels for scoring only; no model was refitted, no new prediction inference was run, and no target-derived threshold, centering transformation or label mapping replaced the frozen outputs. Balanced accuracy remained the equally weighted mean across participants. Pooled confusion counts, proportions of predicted left-hand trials and median stored left-hand probabilities were reported separately as trial-level summaries.
recommended_text.results: The frozen CSP comparator yielded participant-mean balanced accuracies of 51.99% on Cho2017 and 52.77% on Lee2019. In a post-hoc audit of the archived outputs, 92.07% of Cho2017 trials and 83.21% of Lee2019 trials were predicted as left hand; the corresponding pooled median stored left-hand probabilities were 0.669 and 0.633. Pooled confusion matrices showed pronounced class asymmetry rather than uniformly one-class output. These trial-level diagnostics use a different aggregation from the participant-level primary endpoint and did not alter any original prediction.
recommended_text.discussion: The CSP outputs indicate limited transfer and strong class asymmetry under this particular frozen source-trained pipeline. The recorded checks found no disagreement in the declared label mapping, channel selections or deterministic preprocessing implementation, and the original independent audit reproduced the frozen raw-to-prediction results. These checks do not establish the cause of the transfer failure or rule out every acquisition or adapter limitation. Covariance or feature-distribution shifts are plausible explanations, but the present evidence does not isolate them from differences in device, reference, cue timing and preprocessing assumptions. We therefore treat CSP as a contextual comparator and make no general claim of intrinsic CSP inferiority.
recommended_text.supplement_unverified_diagnostics: The separately supplied 10 October 2026 diagnostic report states a 63.04% source resubstitution score, a 61.65% mean score from nine new source-only leave-one-participant-out fits, and 52.39%/54.18% scores after target centering. Trial-level predictions, fold/transform manifests and execution/hash records for these new evaluations were not supplied with the report. These numbers are not part of the independently verified candidate results and are withheld from the scientific results until their evidence chain is available. Resubstitution would not constitute held-out validation; the reported leave-one-participant-out evaluation would add new source fits, and centering derived from target inputs would constitute target adaptation even without target labels.
recommended_text.safe_short_conclusion: Archived-output diagnostics document strong class-asymmetric CSP transfer in this frozen benchmark; they do not prove a unique failure mechanism or the absence of all implementation errors.
